From e4dd748dc87cf431af7b3954963be0d9f6150217 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2022 13:44:21 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: fsl_sai: Fix FSL_SAI_xDR/xFR definition

There are multiple xDR and xFR registers, the index is
from 0 to 7. FSL_SAI_xDR and FSL_SAI_xFR is abandoned,
replace them with FSL_SAI_xDR0 and FSL_SAI_xFR0.

Fixes: 4f7a0728b530 ("ASoC: fsl_sai: Add support for SAI new version")
Signed-off-by: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1653284661-18964-1-git-send-email-shengjiu.wang@nxp.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h b/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
index e4965efe6102..1c8f5ca07f9d 100644
--- a/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
+++ b/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
@@ -80,8 +80,8 @@
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR3(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR3(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR3(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR4(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR4(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR4(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR5(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR5(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR5(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xDR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RDR(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xFR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RFR(ofs))
+#define FSL_SAI_xDR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR0 : FSL_SAI_RDR0)
+#define FSL_SAI_xFR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR0 : FSL_SAI_RFR0)
 #define FSL_SAI_xMR(tx)		(tx ? FSL_SAI_TMR : FSL_SAI_RMR)
 
 /* SAI Transmit/Receive Control Register */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h`**
   - The definitions for `FSL_SAI_xDR` and `FSL_SAI_xFR` have been removed.
   - New definitions `FSL_SAI_xDR0` and `FSL_SAI_xFR0` have been introduced to replace the previous definitions. These new definitions specifically reference the 0th index of the transmit and receive data registers.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `fsl_sai.h` file address a bug related to the handling of multiple xDR and xFR registers, which are indexed from 0 to 7. By abandoning the generic `FSL_SAI_xDR` and `FSL_SAI_xFR` definitions and replacing them with `FSL_SAI_xDR0` and `FSL_SAI_xFR0`, the patch ensures that the code correctly references the intended registers, thereby fixing the issue introduced in a previous commit (identified by the fix reference). This change enhances clarity and correctness in the register definitions used in the driver.

Here is the commit message:
ASoC: fsl_sai: Fix FSL_SAI_xDR/xFR definition

There are multiple xDR and xFR registers, the index is
from 0 to 7. FSL_SAI_xDR and FSL_SAI_xFR is abandoned,
replace them with FSL_SAI_xDR0 and FSL_SAI_xFR0.

Fixes: 4f7a0728b530 ("ASoC: fsl_sai: Add support for SAI new version")
Signed-off-by: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1653284661-18964-1-git-send-email-shengjiu.wang@nxp.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the use of generic definitions `FSL_SAI_xDR` and `FSL_SAI_xFR`, which did not specify the register index, leading to ambiguity when accessing multiple xDR and xFR registers indexed from 0 to 7. This could result in incorrect register access and functionality issues in the driver.

Here is the patch:
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR4(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR4(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR4(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR5(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR5(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR5(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xDR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RDR(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xFR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RFR(ofs))
+#define FSL_SAI_xDR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR0 : FSL_SAI_RDR0)
+#define FSL_SAI_xFR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR0 : FSL_SAI_RFR0)
 #define FSL_SAI_xMR(tx)		(tx ? FSL_SAI_TMR : FSL_SAI_RMR)

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define FSL_SAI_xDR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RDR(ofs))
#define FSL_SAI_xFR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RFR(ofs))
```
Reason:
The use of generic definitions `FSL_SAI_xDR` and `FSL_SAI_xFR` without specifying the register index leads to ambiguity when accessing multiple xDR and xFR registers (indexed from 0 to 7). This can cause incorrect register access, resulting in functionality issues in the driver.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define FSL_SAI_xDR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR0 : FSL_SAI_RDR0)
#define FSL_SAI_xFR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR0 : FSL_SAI_RFR0)
```
Reason:
The patch replaces the ambiguous generic definitions with specific definitions `FSL_SAI_xDR0` and `FSL_SAI_xFR0`, which explicitly refer to the register index 0. This eliminates the ambiguity and ensures correct access to the intended registers, thereby fixing the functionality issues in the driver.
